I made scribe for your lectures. Here’s where everything is. Try a short recording first, so you can get a feel for it.

In Library, tap Record a lecture and allow the microphone. Pause and Resume keep the same recording. Tap ★ Important when you want to find a moment later. Stop finishes the recording and starts transcription. Try recording with the screen off once before a real lecture; the notification also has recording controls. For a lecture, keep the microphone uncovered and place the tablet as close to the speaker as practical. Make a short trial and listen to it before relying on a long recording; distant speech masked by room noise may remain unintelligible.

Text appears after you stop recording. Choose Lecture at the top of Library for the stronger recognizer; supported languages are identified automatically. Compatibility keeps the older recognizer and fixed-language choices. Pause transcription waits for the current bounded section before stopping; Continue resumes saved progress. Open a lecture to see progress. Numbers are underlined in Lecture mode so you can check them. Medical terms and numbers can still be wrong: tap a passage to listen and hold it to correct the text. More → Transcribe again creates a separate transcript from all retained audio, using the mode selected in Library; original text and corrections stay unchanged.

Library keeps your lectures. Search looks through course names, titles and saved text; the course and date filters narrow the list. Add / change course assigns a lecture afterwards. In Courses, tap a course to open it or hold to rename it. More → Rename lecture changes a lecture title.

Tap a text passage to hear its audio. Hold it to correct the words, then Save. Important moments takes you back to your ★ marks once that part is transcribed. More → Stop playback stops listening. If the audio has been deleted, its text is still there.

Import audio opens your file picker. Choose a recording already saved on your tablet for offline use. Keep the original where it is: scribe needs access to it for transcription and playback. Imported originals are never deleted by scribe.

Copy text puts the transcript on your clipboard. Export TXT saves a text file where you choose. More → Share text sends it through another app. More → Delete lecture removes that lecture’s saved text and recordings from scribe; an imported original stays untouched. Export text you want to keep first.

App language changes the menus between English and Romanian. Transcription mode at the top of Library or in Settings applies to new recordings and imports. Lecture mode recognises 25 European languages automatically, including Romanian and English. Compatibility offers the previous language selector: choose Romanian or English when known, or Auto. Existing lectures keep their original recognizer and text. Show timestamps controls times in text and exports. Dark theme changes the colours.

Lecture mode always keeps recordings for checking. Compatibility also keeps audio by default. Delete successfully transcribed audio applies only to new Compatibility recordings, after completion without errors or review warnings. Checks cannot detect every mistake. Deleted audio cannot be restored; text and marks remain, and imported originals are never deleted. Transcribe again requires all source audio to remain available.

If a lecture needs attention, open it and read the message. Make space or let the tablet cool down if asked, then tap Continue transcription. A sudden shutdown can lose the unfinished bit of a recording. Your completed sections and saved text remain. The app works locally, with no account or cloud backup.
10. When I send you an update

Open the new APK and install it over scribe. Keep the existing app installed: uninstalling it or clearing its data deletes local recordings and text. Updates need your confirmation. A short window explains what changed. Settings → Patch notes keeps the update history.
If something looks wrong, send me a screenshot and tell me what you tapped.
